name: severino-vault-mcp
description: Local stdio MCP server for Joe's Obsidian vaults. With no subcommand it serves MCP; subcommands run one governed call against the labs vault (or the named dataset) and print JSON.

global_options.name: --fingerprint
global_options.help: Print a hash of the binary's Go sources and exit. tools compares the installed binary with the source tree to detect a stale install.

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Validate configured vault frontmatter without starting the MCP server.

args.name: --propose
args.help: Print starter frontmatter for markdown files that are missing it.

commands.name: touch-reviewed
commands.summary: Set last_reviewed to today on a vault doc and print JSON. Exits 0 if ok, 1 otherwise.

args.name: relative_path
args.help: Vault-relative path, e.g. '03 Runbooks/Generate Internal Service Certificate.md'.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: backfill-aliases
commands.summary: Set each folder-note's (`<folder>/index.md`) Obsidian `aliases` to its `title`, so `[[Title]]` resolves and autocompletes for notes whose filename is the non-unique `index`. Derived from `title`, so idempotent — safe to re-run to repair drift. Writeups are left alone.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: find
commands.summary: Section-scoped vault search: ranked hits, each with its best-matching section (heading, slug, one-line summary), never a body.

args.name: query
args.help: Natural-language query, e.g. 'renew the TLS cert'.

args.name: --limit
args.help: Maximum hits to return (default 5, capped at 25).

args.name: --fields
args.help: Hit fields to print, as dotted paths (e.g. doc_id title snippets.text); omit for every field.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: read
commands.summary: Read one vault doc by doc_id and print JSON. With --sections, return just those sections (the token-minimal path); without it, the whole body. Honors the sensitivity gate — restricted bodies are withheld (no interactive unlock on the CLI path).

args.name: doc_id
args.help: Stable doc_id, e.g. 'rb-add-nginx-proxy-host'.

args.name: --sections
args.help: Section slugs or heading paths from a `find` hit or the outline. Omit for the whole body.

args.name: --fields
args.help: Doc fields to print (e.g. outline for the section list without text); omit for every field.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: task-list
commands.summary: The backlog board: every `doc_type: task` doc, derived from the index (project tasks under 01 Projects/<project>/tasks/ + the 07 Backlog/ cross-cutting bucket), filtered and ranked. Default shows live work (open + active); the thin `backlog` CLI and the Obsidian cockpit render this — the MCP is the one task brain.

args.name: --status
args.help: Only this status.

args.name: --project
args.help: Only this project (folder or related_projects).

args.name: --stale-only
args.help: Only stale (open/active, untouched past the window).

args.name: --all
args.help: Include parked/done/wontfix.

args.name: --stale-days
args.help: Stale window in days (default 14).

args.name: --limit
args.help: Most tasks to print, best first (default 0: all).

args.name: --fields
args.help: Task fields to print (e.g. doc_id title status); omit for the whole board.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: promote-note
commands.summary: Promote a captured note (e.g. an 00 Inbox/ capture) into a task, preserving its body and deleting the source. The capture → task half of the inbox loop; used by the Obsidian promote command.

args.name: source
args.help: Vault-relative path to the note.

args.name: --title
args.help: Task title.

args.name: --project
args.help: Owning project (colocates the task).

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: update-frontmatter
commands.summary: Set fields in a vault doc's frontmatter: the MCP set_frontmatter tool, one flag per field the labs profile declares, each validated against it (doc_id never changes once set). Used by the Obsidian relation editor so author-time edits can't dangle.

args.name: relative_path
args.help: Vault-relative path to the doc.

args.name: --doc-id
args.help: Stable id; required to create, and fixed once set. Unique across docs.

args.name: --title
args.help: The doc's title.

args.name: --doc-type
args.help: What kind of doc this is. One of the vault's doc_type values.

args.name: --system
args.help: The system the doc is about.

args.name: --environment
args.help: Where that system runs. One of the vault's environment values.

args.name: --status
args.help: The doc's lifecycle state (a task's own lifecycle for tasks). One of the vault's status values.

args.name: --sensitivity
args.help: Who may read the body. One of the vault's sensitivity values.

args.name: --last-reviewed
args.help: When the doc was last checked against reality. ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

args.name: --touch-last-reviewed
args.help: Set last_reviewed to today.

args.name: --set-tags
args.help: Replace tags: tags.

args.name: --add-tags
args.help: Append to tags.

args.name: --remove-tags
args.help: Remove from tags (update only).

args.name: --set-related-projects
args.help: Replace related_projects: projects the doc belongs to, as folder names under the projects folder.

args.name: --add-related-projects
args.help: Append to related_projects.

args.name: --remove-related-projects
args.help: Remove from related_projects (update only).

args.name: --set-related-assets
args.help: Replace related_assets: assets the doc touches.

args.name: --add-related-assets
args.help: Append to related_assets.

args.name: --remove-related-assets
args.help: Remove from related_assets (update only).

args.name: --set-aliases
args.help: Replace aliases: other names Obsidian resolves links by.

args.name: --add-aliases
args.help: Append to aliases.

args.name: --remove-aliases
args.help: Remove from aliases (update only).

args.name: --effort
args.help: A task's size. One of the vault's effort values.

args.name: --priority
args.help: A task's priority. One of the vault's priority values.

args.name: --created
args.help: When a task was filed. ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

args.name: --closed
args.help: When a task was finished. ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

args.name: --project-path
args.help: Where the project's working copy lives on this machine. An absolute path or one under ~/. E.g. ~/Code/Projects/example. Only on 01 Projects/*/index.md.

args.name: --set-repos
args.help: Replace repos: repository directory names whose sessions use this project's work queue (see the queue tool). A bare repository directory name, with no "/". Unique across docs. E.g. example-repo. Only on 01 Projects/*/index.md.

args.name: --add-repos
args.help: Append to repos.

args.name: --remove-repos
args.help: Remove from repos (update only).

args.name: --queue-prefix
args.help: The id prefix of this project's work queue items. Lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter, at most 12 characters. Unique across docs. E.g. hq. Only on 01 Projects/*/index.md.

args.name: --superseded-by
args.help: The doc_id of the doc that replaces this one; the older report of a series carries it with status: deprecated. E.g. report-example-audit-2026-10-01.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: write-doc
commands.summary: Create a registered doc, or replace or append to one section of its body, with the markdown body on stdin (no frontmatter). The MCP write_doc tool: create validates the new frontmatter with the rules validate checks; section modes keep the frontmatter except last_reviewed, which becomes today. Restricted docs are refused.

args.name: --mode
args.help: create (default), replace_section or append_section.

args.name: --relative-path
args.help: Vault-relative path; required to create.

args.name: --doc-id
args.help: The new doc's id on create; the doc to edit otherwise.

args.name: --heading
args.help: Exact heading text of the section to edit (section modes); "" for the text before the first heading.

args.name: --title
args.help: The doc's title.

args.name: --doc-type
args.help: What kind of doc this is. One of the vault's doc_type values.

args.name: --system
args.help: The system the doc is about.

args.name: --environment
args.help: Where that system runs. One of the vault's environment values.

args.name: --status
args.help: The doc's lifecycle state (a task's own lifecycle for tasks). One of the vault's status values.

args.name: --sensitivity
args.help: Who may read the body. One of the vault's sensitivity values.

args.name: --last-reviewed
args.help: When the doc was last checked against reality. ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

args.name: --tags
args.help: Replace tags: tags.

args.name: --related-projects
args.help: Replace related_projects: projects the doc belongs to, as folder names under the projects folder.

args.name: --related-assets
args.help: Replace related_assets: assets the doc touches.

args.name: --aliases
args.help: Replace aliases: other names Obsidian resolves links by.

args.name: --effort
args.help: A task's size. One of the vault's effort values.

args.name: --priority
args.help: A task's priority. One of the vault's priority values.

args.name: --created
args.help: When a task was filed. ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

args.name: --closed
args.help: When a task was finished. ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

args.name: --project-path
args.help: Where the project's working copy lives on this machine. An absolute path or one under ~/. E.g. ~/Code/Projects/example. Only on 01 Projects/*/index.md.

args.name: --repos
args.help: Replace repos: repository directory names whose sessions use this project's work queue (see the queue tool). A bare repository directory name, with no "/". Unique across docs. E.g. example-repo. Only on 01 Projects/*/index.md.

args.name: --queue-prefix
args.help: The id prefix of this project's work queue items. Lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter, at most 12 characters. Unique across docs. E.g. hq. Only on 01 Projects/*/index.md.

args.name: --superseded-by
args.help: The doc_id of the doc that replaces this one; the older report of a series carries it with status: deprecated. E.g. report-example-audit-2026-10-01.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: move-doc
commands.summary: Move or rename a registered doc, keeping its doc_id and frontmatter: the MCP move_doc tool. Refuses a destination that exists, one outside the indexed folders or in a read-only one, and a file name another note already has; lists the notes whose [[links]] named the old location.

args.name: to
args.help: Destination from the vault root: a .md path, or a folder ending in / to keep the file name.

args.name: --doc-id
args.help: The doc to move.

args.name: --relative-path
args.help: The doc's current vault-relative path (instead of --doc-id).

args.name: --with-folder
args.help: Move the doc's whole folder, files beside it included, into the destination folder.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: log-entries
commands.summary: List an append-only log note's entries (one top-level bullet each), or close one by appending ' → <resolution>' to its line. The MCP log_entries tool: close needs --match to name exactly one open entry, and writes like a section edit.

args.name: action
args.help: list or close.

args.name: doc_id
args.help: The log note's doc_id.

args.name: --all
args.help: list: include closed entries.

args.name: --contains
args.help: list: only entries whose text contains this (case-insensitive).

args.name: --limit
args.help: list: most entries to print, in file order (default 0: all).

args.name: --match
args.help: close: text that exactly one open entry contains.

args.name: --resolution
args.help: close: one line saying how the entry was resolved.

args.name: --fields
args.help: Entry fields to print (line, text, closed, resolution); omit for every field.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: queue
commands.summary: Add, list, set, claim, close or promote work items in a project's queue (01 Projects/<project>/Queue.md, or 07 Backlog/Queue.md) and print compact JSON; the MCP queue tool. Hooks call it: name the queue with --cwd, and pass a value that starts with a dash as --flag=value. Exits 0 if ok, 1 on a refused call, 2 on a usage error.

args.name: action
args.help: list, add, set, close or promote.

args.name: id
args.help: set, close, promote: the item's id, e.g. example-3.

args.name: --project
args.help: The queue's project folder under 01 Projects, or backlog.

args.name: --repo
args.help: A repository directory name, resolved through each project's index.md repos.

args.name: --cwd
args.help: A working directory, resolved to its repository and then its project.

args.name: --all
args.help: list: every queue.

args.name: --agent
args.help: add: the worker's agent id. list: that agent's items. set, close, promote: the item by agent.

args.name: --kind
args.help: add: next, delegated, decision or follow-up. list: only this kind.

args.name: --text
args.help: add: one line saying what the work is. set: replace it.

args.name: --owner
args.help: add, set: who holds the item ('' or - for nobody). list: that owner's items.

args.name: --pr
args.help: Link: a PR number or URL ('' removes it on set).

args.name: --branch
args.help: Link: a branch.

args.name: --commit
args.help: Link: commits, comma-separated.

args.name: --slug
args.help: Link: a content slug.

args.name: --blocked-by
args.help: add, set: item ids that must close first.

args.name: --status
args.help: set: open, returned or parked. close: closed (default) or dropped. list: comma-separated statuses or all (default open,returned).

args.name: --ready
args.help: list: open next and follow-up items whose blockers are all closed or dropped.

args.name: --contains
args.help: list: items whose text contains this (case-insensitive).

args.name: --limit
args.help: list: most items to print (default 0: all).

args.name: --claim
args.help: set: take the item for --owner only if nobody holds it.

args.name: --resolution
args.help: close: one line, e.g. repo@sha, a PR, a doc id, or why it was dropped.

args.name: --content
args.help: promote: the body doc's markdown.

args.name: --fields
args.help: list: item fields to print (id, project, kind, status, owner, text, links, blocked_by, body, alias, agent, resolution); omit for every field.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: task-reconcile
commands.summary: Re-home tasks into tasks/ (live) or tasks/done/ (closed) per their status — the idempotent tidy sweep for statuses edited by hand (a Base/Properties edit) that didn't move through task-move.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: task-projects
commands.summary: The task-project universe: every 01 Projects/<project>/ folder a task can be filed in, with its open-task count. The one owner of where a task can go — pickers (the Obsidian modal, the cockpit) derive from this instead of re-walking the vault layout.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: task-add
commands.summary: Author a new task file. With --project it colocates at 01 Projects/<project>/tasks/ and links related_projects; without, it files a cross-cutting task in 07 Backlog/. Schema-validated, written through the one atomic serializer.

args.name: title
args.help: Imperative task title.

args.name: --project
args.help: Owning project (an 01 Projects/<project>/ folder).

args.name: --related-projects
args.help: Projects a cross-cutting task touches.

args.name: --effort
args.help: Effort S|M|L (default S).

args.name: --priority
args.help: Priority high|med|low (default med).

args.name: --tags
args.help: Tags (default: backlog).

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: task-delete
commands.summary: Permanently delete a task file (for mistakes / junk only — finished or abandoned work should be task-move'd to done/wontfix, which keeps it queryable). Resolves a bare slug or the full id; refuses non-tasks.

args.name: doc_id
args.help: Task id or slug (task-foo or foo).

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: task-move
commands.summary: Move a task to a new status (open|active|parked|done|wontfix). Stamps closed: on done, clears it on reopen; done tasks are kept so 'what shipped' stays a query. Resolves a bare slug or the full id.

args.name: doc_id
args.help: Task id or slug (task-foo or foo).

args.name: status
args.help: Target status (open|active|parked|done|wontfix).

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: hq-manifest
commands.summary: Build the Severino HQ manifest with the package's shared frontmatter parser.

args.name: vault
args.help: Vault root path.

args.name: subdirs
args.help: Colon-separated vault subdirectories to index. Default: derived from the MCP config's indexed_dirs plus the slim content dirs (05 Writeups, 06 Pages) — one list, one owner.

args.name: --report
args.help: Print the full result (missing_frontmatter, duplicates, counts) as JSON instead of the manifest entries. Backs `hq doctor`.

commands.name: brief
commands.summary: Doc-side vault state in one payload: recent changes, docs overdue for review, and inbox backlog. The vault leg of the `brief` shell tool.

args.name: --days
args.help: Recent-changes look-back window in days (default 7).

args.name: --review-after
args.help: Flag docs whose last_reviewed is older than N days (default 180).

args.name: --limit
args.help: Max recent commits to return (default 15).

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Indent the JSON output.

commands.name: schema
commands.summary: Emit the canonical frontmatter schema (enum sets) as JSON. Severino HQ commits this output and validates against it so the two systems share one definition.

args.name: --json
args.help: Emit the schema as JSON (the default).

args.name: --contract
args.help: Emit the complete versioned profile contract, including task and per-document rules. The legacy default remains HQ-compatible.

args.name: --fingerprint
args.help: Emit the stable SHA-256 fingerprint of the complete profile contract.

args.name: --json-schema
args.help: Emit a vault's frontmatter rules as a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for off-the-shelf validators and editors, derived from the profile set_frontmatter and validate use.

args.name: --vault
args.help: With --json-schema: the vault whose profile to emit, labs (default) or edu.

args.name: --check-doc
args.help: Instead of emitting, verify that a human schema doc's enum lines (doc_type/environment/status/sensitivity) match the canonical schema. Exit 1 and print mismatches on drift.

commands.name: daily-write
commands.summary: Replace the generated brief region of a daily note (markdown on stdin): the marked MIRROR:daily-brief span only, leaving the free-capture area untouched. Creates the note from the daily-note frontmatter contract if absent. The write behind tools' `vault daily`.

args.name: --date
args.help: Daily note date (YYYY-MM-DD; default today).

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: export
commands.summary: Emit a vault's publishable dataset as JSON. `education`: institutions and courses with their `## Site` bullets, read by jseverino.com and resume-engine.

args.name: dataset
args.help: Dataset to emit.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: validate
commands.summary: Check vault docs' frontmatter with the rules set_frontmatter writes by, without the MCP server: one `<relative_path>: <problem>` line per problem, exit 1 on any. Paths outside the labs and edu vaults' indexed dirs (read-only folders such as 00 Inbox, 05 Writeups and 06 Pages included), or not markdown, are ignored, so an editor or agent hook can pass every edited path.

args.name: path
args.help: Doc path, absolute or relative to a vault root.

args.name: --json
args.help: Print {"ok": ..., "problems": [{"relative_path", "problem"}]} instead of lines.

commands.name: describe
commands.summary: Emit this repo's command surface as structured JSON: every subcommand, its arguments, and help, generated from the command table itself so it can't drift from --help. AI reads it; a TUI renders a command picker.

args.name: --pretty
args.help: Pretty-print JSON with indentation (default: compact).

commands.name: serve
commands.summary: Serve MCP over stdio. The default with no subcommand.
